summary.headline: Airfloa H1 FY26 net profit rose 24% YoY to INR12.09 crore on INR90.98 crore total income; order book crossed INR455 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY26 total income of INR90.98 crore (up nearly 7% YoY), EBITDA of INR22.46 crore and net profit of INR12.09 crore (up 24% YoY), its first results call after the BSE SME listing in September 2025. Active order book was stated at over INR455 crore after a recent INR1,013 crore order win in a single week from ICF and MCF. Management guided to FY26 turnover of over INR300 crore and FY27 of at least INR550 crore, with defence (drones, anti-drone, laser systems via a JV with Big Bang Boom Solutions) as a stated growth driver. Capacity is being expanded through a 14-acre plant purchase, with a term loan under discussion.

financial_highlights.metric: Net profit margin (as referenced by analyst)

financial_highlights.change: crossed after recent wins; includes about INR65 crore defence

segments.name: Railways (govt and non-govt)
segments.commentary: Management put railway orders at about INR390-405 crore of the book, 75-80% from Indian Railways and 20% from non-government customers. Key programmes cited include Vande Bharat, LHB, Amrit Bharat and metro work.

segments.name: Defence and aerospace
segments.commentary: Defence order book about INR65 crore. Management expects INR100-120 crore of defence revenue in FY27 from a new INR200-250 crore order intake. Products cited: tether drone, loitering drone, anti-drone laser systems, radar, unmanned land systems, MBT hulls and aerospace simulators. Entered defence in 2020.

guidance_outlook: FY26 turnover guided at over INR300 crore; management said up to INR310 crore is committed, with 300-350 crore possible.
FY27 revenue guided at a minimum of INR550 crore, with INR500 crore+ cited on paper; management called 550 the bare minimum.
Q3 FY26 revenue indicated at INR70-75 crore and Q4 at about INR120 crore; Q4 typically 40-45% of annual turnover.
Management said defence could reach about 50% of revenue within two years, and that margins should improve as defence scales.
Management said the order book could reach about INR1,000 crore by March 2026 and that a further INR30 crore of orders was expected in the near term.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation about 85% on each of two shifts after moving from single shift in September 2025.
A 14-acre plant is being bought; a first facility of 50,000 sq ft is targeted by end-December 2026, scaling to about 1 lakh sq ft; land settlement expected by January 2026.
Planned new facility capex INR20-30 crore to start; management expects asset turnover of about 4x the investment.
Plan to set up a facility near MCF and RCF to cut transport costs; term loan talks with banks under way.
Defence capex of INR100-150 crore over 1-1.5 years; INR6-7 crore already invested in prototyping, with INR25-30 crore planned over the next 6-7 months.
Capex deviation: machine model changed with vendor PONC, saving about INR22 lakh.
demand_pricing: Management said it takes only contracts that meet its margin threshold; PAT margin of about 12% cited by an analyst, with management aiming to improve margins through defence mix.
Door systems (Vande Bharat focus) and vacuum toilet systems named as near-term products; orders expected to be announced in the following weeks.
Six products in development across railways (security, surveillance, fire suppression, doors, vacuum toilets); two have development orders.
Kavach-type integrated train security system to be exhibited next financial year; approval needs RDSO/Railway Board trials of 9-12 months.
Certifications cited: about 52 defence labs (CVRDE, ARDE, DRDO labs), STANAG certificate, and AI (aerospace) certification enabling supply to HAL and ADA.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR455 crore book is rail versus defence, and what is the execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence is about INR65 crore; the rest is rail, both government and non-government. INR200-250 crore is to execute within this year, running to December of next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 12% PAT margins sustainable, and is there scope for improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not take contracts below its margin threshold and is trying to lift margins, helped by defence traction; no numerical margin target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Big Bang Boom JV and how much is being invested?
qa_highlights.answer: A JV with Airfloa holding a majority stake, focused on high-power laser anti-drone systems (2,000-5,000 m range) and an autonomous drone programme. Details were deferred to a later presentation, citing compliance constraints.

qa_highlights.question: What capacity and capex are needed to deliver FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current shift expansion gives about INR300 crore; the new facility (INR20-30 crore capex, funded by term loan) is expected to take revenue to INR500 crore+ from January 2027 onward.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence capex need and funding plan?
qa_highlights.answer: INR100-150 crore over 1-1.5 years for drone and anti-drone systems, to be recycled and supplemented by a separate fundraise later. Around 25-30% is planned by March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the IPO proceeds are unutilised?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18% of IPO proceeds remain unutilised; the deviation relates to a machine model change with the same vendor.

risks_watch: Execution risk: FY26 target of INR300 crore+ needs about INR200 crore in H2 (about INR91 crore delivered in H1), with capacity at about 85% on double shift.
Capacity constraint until the new 50,000 sq ft facility (targeted end-December 2026); FY27 INR550 crore guidance depends on it.
Defence scale-up depends on tenders, trials and certifications; management said several products are awaiting trials, and the JV's contribution is not yet quantified.
Working capital and funding: term loan not yet sanctioned; another equity fundraise is planned in about 1.5 years.
Disclosure risk: management deferred several details (the six products, the Big Bang Boom JV, door-system empanelment) to later announcements.
Several figures varied across answers (for example, railway book INR390 vs 405 crore, and the FY27 defence figure), so the numbers need confirmation against filings.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on order flow and growth targets, with repeated numerical commitments. Evasive on defence specifics and JV terms, citing compliance and deferring detail to later presentations. Some answers were imprecise or contradictory, for example on capacity utilisation and the timing of Kavach approvals.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says it turns down contracts below its margin threshold and expects defence mix to lift margins from about 12% PAT, but gave no numerical target and the JV is not quantified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: A 14-acre plant is being bought and a first 50,000 sq ft facility is targeted by end-December 2026, scaling to about 1 lakh sq ft, while utilisation is already about 85% on two shifts.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue guided to rise from about INR300 crore in FY26 to at least INR550 crore in FY27, with H1 FY26 total income up only about 7% YoY, so growth depends on the new facility from January 2027.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 85% on each of two shifts, and a INR20-30 crore facility plus INR100-150 crore defence capex are planned, with term loan talks under way but not sanctioned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Active order book is over INR455 crore after a INR1,013 crore order win, and FY26 committed level was raised to around INR310 crore, but the defence pipeline is still awaiting trials and tenders.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 needs about INR200 crore in H2 against about INR91 crore delivered in H1, and FY27's INR550 crore minimum depends on a facility not yet built and a term loan not yet sanctioned.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Door systems and vacuum toilet systems orders are expected in the following weeks, and six products are in development with two holding development orders, though Kavach-type approval needs 9-12 months of trials.

rows.label: Defence order intake INR200-250 crore
rows.why: Management expects INR100-120 crore of defence revenue in FY27 from a new INR200-250 crore order intake, but the defence book is only about INR65 crore and depends on tenders and trials.

rows.label: Defence scale-up to 50% of revenue
rows.why: Management says defence could reach about 50% of revenue within two years, backed by drone, anti-drone and laser products with the Big Bang Boom JV, though JV economics are undisclosed.

rows.label: Term loan and equity raise
rows.why: Term loan talks are under way for the new facility and another equity fundraise is planned in about 1.5 years, with INR100-150 crore defence capex to be funded.

tone.note: Management was confident on order flow, the INR550 crore FY27 minimum and the end-December 2026 facility, but evasive on defence specifics and JV terms; analysts pressed on the 12% PAT margin sustainability and the funding of capacity.

quality.why: Brief gives H1 FY26 total income up nearly 7% and net profit up 24% YoY but does not state what drove growth (volume, price or mix), and names no one-off items; profit growth outpacing income suggests margin gains, but the brief gives no cause.
